title: Can a row of numbers grow by just one, or by twenty, each time?
description: Kavya's father sells bus tickets in Chennai and finds rows of serial numbers with some missing. The video finds the rule of four rows, small ones too.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rule can be small, and the whole gap must be used. Watch for children who read one digit of the gap, like the tens digit.

source: Let Us Do 1 (d), (e), (f), (g), continue the patterns
video_script.why: The child has met rules like one hundred and now meets rows that grow by twenty, by one and by two, crossing a round number.
video_script.substitution: Find the whole gap between neighbours, test it, then add it again to go on, watching the hundreds when a row crosses a round number.
video_script.anchor: serial numbers on bus ticket books sold by Kavya's father in Chennai, some torn out
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu sees the tens digit go from zero to two in the second row and says the rule is add two. The real gap is twenty.
video_script.payoff_line: the rule is add one hundred

final_answer.spoken: add one hundred, add twenty, add one, add two

never_show: the answer rows before the idea part
maths_rules: slip: add 2 on row e would give 10,105 + 2 = 10,107, not 10,125
video_script.design: Exercise: four rows with small rules. Hint: use two neighbours. Four rows of serial numbers sit on the stage; the gaps arrive as labels in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Kavya's father sells bus tickets in Chennai. Each ticket has a serial number, and some tickets are torn out.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first row climbs from ten thousand one hundred to ten thousand nine hundred. Its middle numbers are missing.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second row has ten thousand one hundred five, then ten thousand one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The third row has ten thousand nine hundred ninety two, then ten thousand nine hundred ninety three.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The last row goes ten thousand seven hundred ninety four and ten thousand seven hundred ninety six. Then comes ten thousand seven hundred ninety eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Continue each row.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the four rows stay; two neighbouring numbers in the second row are circled; the words the gap may be small appear

marks.pair: two neighbouring numbers in the second row are circled
marks.small: the words the gap may be small appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>Take two numbers that sit side by side and find the whole gap.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The gap can be small, so check every digit of it.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Use the gap to fill the blanks. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows add 2 beside the second row; the tens digits 0 and 2 are circled; the line 10,105 + 2 = 10,107 appears and is crossed out; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.strike: the line is crossed out and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>In the second row, the tens digit goes from zero to two, so the rule is add two.
<bookmark mark='test'/>That reads one digit only. Ten thousand one hundred five add two makes ten thousand one hundred seven.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is not the next number in the row.

beats.on_screen: row d gets the gap label +100 and its blanks fill 10,400 to 10,800; row e gets the board line 10,125 − 10,105 = 20 and the blanks fill with 10,145 and 10,165

marks.drule: the rule card add 100 appears and the middle numbers fill in
marks.e: the second row gets the label gap 20

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>In the first row, ten thousand two hundred take away ten thousand one hundred leaves one hundred.
<bookmark mark='drule'/>The rule is add one hundred. The missing numbers go from ten thousand four hundred up to ten thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='e'/>In the second row, the two numbers are twenty apart. The rule is add twenty.
<bookmark mark='efill'/>Add twenty twice to reach ten thousand one hundred forty five and ten thousand one hundred sixty five.

beats.on_screen: row f gets the gap label +1 and fills 10,994 and 10,995; row g gets the gap label +2 and fills 10,800 and 10,802; the hundreds digit of row g flips from 7 to 8

marks.f: the third row gets the gap label +1
marks.g: the fourth row gets the gap label +2
marks.gfill: the first blank fills with 10,800 and the hundreds digit flips from 7 to 8

narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>In the third row, the gap is one, so the rule is add one.
<bookmark mark='ffill'/>The next two numbers are ten thousand nine hundred ninety four and ten thousand nine hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='g'/>In the last row, the gap is two, so the rule is add two.
<bookmark mark='gfill'/>Ten thousand seven hundred ninety eight add two makes ten thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='gone'/>Add two again to reach ten thousand eight hundred two.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the ticket book; the lines start at the first number, add the rule step by step, watch the round numbers appear

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>To check, start at the first number of a row and add the rule step by step.
<bookmark mark='land'/>You must land on each number that the row already gives.
<bookmark mark='round'/>Watch the hundreds digit when a row crosses a round number such as ten thousand eight hundred.
